newsitem.title: FRANCE: INSTANT VIEW - French Q3 GDP up 0.9 pct.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - French Q3 GDP up 0.9 pct.

text.p: Following are analysts' comments on the 0.9 percent preliminary rise in third quarter gross domestic product in France, reported by INSEE.
It is a little higher than the market consensus but as INSEE is reporting the number of working days this probably weighed in favour of such a higher figure.

If we look at other compenents, in terms of private consumption: the fairly active rebound on the back of the end of the car incentive scheme...and also we had relatively hefty consumer spending in Q3 due to households running down their savings ratio.

I don't think it will move the market that much. The data is broadly in line with expectations. But investment actually rose one percent in Q3 and this is a good surprise after three consecutive falls which had taken the market by surprise in the previous quarters.
CHRISTOPHER POTTS, CHIEF ECONOMIST, CHEUVREUX DE VIRIEU -

It's in line with expectations; there's nothing very surprising here: personal consumption up in large part of because of the car incentive scheme ending, a positive trade contribution, stocks still down.

(Asked about the Q3 rise in investment): If there is any component that gets revised it is the investment number. It is a very fragile first estimate. After the news we have had over the past year it is to be taken with some caution, I think. We don't have any indication yet there is any great turnaround here -- that will be the last component of demand to turn.

The overall picture is that as in Germany, the economy has touched bottom. We will have a weak fourth quarter in terms of numbers. I think the number will be flat. It is not even impossible that we could have a negative GDP number in the fourth quarter, but it doesn't change the big picture. Annualised growth is about two percent in the second half of this year.

PATRICK MANGE, DEUTSCHE BANK ECONOMIST, PARIS - Q3 mostly matches forecasts. What is interesting is Q2 was revised by 0.2 percent as well. With even a flat fourth quarter we could have 1.1 to 1.2 percent growth for 1996 and maybe somewhat higher because we have an acquired growth now. It is difficult to say what can be achieved in the fourth quarter (after benefit of working days and expiry of car scheme in Q3). At the first readings from consumption we expect consumption to be down on a basis effect but other compenents like business investment are very difficult to forecast. We could come out best at 0.1 percent in Q4 but we could equally drop by 0.2 percent.
